days.title: Day 1 — Understand Onesa
objectives: Explain Onesa UG and its products.
Identify frontend API worker database model and documentation providers.
Distinguish public engineering and private release evidence.
checkpoints: Select each product in the ecosystem diagram and open its reference.
Name one staging-only capability and one planned hardware capability.
Find the canonical runbook and restricted evidence boundary.

days.title: Day 2 — Understand the software
objectives: Trace one endpoint from frontend to API schema and storage.
Explain session CSRF roles and ownership.
Prepare isolated development without production data.
checkpoints: Choose an endpoint in the API explorer and identify its request/response model.
Find the owner foreign key in a generated ERD.
Run publication hygiene locally and use synthetic development fixtures.

days.title: Day 3 — Understand delivery
objectives: Explain dev → staging → main and actual workflow entry points.
Match a CI run to its source revision and provider deployment.
Recognize failures and the rollback boundary.
checkpoints: Read deploy.yml and release-candidate.yml in their owning repositories.
Explain why private GitHub Free protection cannot be assumed.
Describe recovery after a failed hosted check without skipping it.

days.title: Day 4 — Understand operations
objectives: Read health and scanner status without revealing secrets.
Locate monitoring backup restore and incident runbooks.
checkpoints: Use ssh -O check onesa-portal-worker from authorized owner setup.
Inspect only redacted status; never compose config without --quiet.
Identify the isolated restore command and on-call owner escalation path.
